thread:
maria: Quick share — ran fused vs paged Flash variants on A100 (drivers from last stable). Observed a consistent 8-12% slowdown when using INTERLEAVED KV layout vs SEPARATE at seq_len=2048, batch=16. Small/no diff at seq<=512. Dumping outputs below.

aj: ugh. can you paste the perf numbers or a flamegraph link?

maria: pasted key numbers, short:
```
Model: gpt-like-7B
HW: A100-80GB, cuda 12.1
config: batch=16, seq=2048, dtype=fp16

fused-flash (SEPARATE KV):  43.2 ms/token
paged-flash (SEPARATE KV):  46.5 ms/token
fused-flash (INTERLEAVED KV): 47.1 ms/token  <-- ~9.1% regression vs fused separate
paged-flash (INTERLEAVED KV): 49.8 ms/token

perf-bot nightly baseline (2026-11-18): fused separate @ 43.0 ms/token
```
Also grabbed a microtrace showing scattered gld/stores in the KV read path when interleaved.

kevin: likely alignment + stride issues. interleaved layout changes memory stride for KV per-head: head_stride went from 64B -> 128B in our packing after the refactor. That can break coalescing and hurt warp efficiency, especially for fused kernels that expect contiguous heads.

sophie: FYI I pointed at PR 5243 last week — it changed packing order to pack head-major then seq-major, which reduced cpu copy work but might have increased GPU stride. @maria can you repro with the older packing quickly?

maria: i re-ran with a patched binary reversing that PR packing on the KV side — regression disappears, fused interleaved matches separate within 1-2%. So PR 5243 looks suspicious.

aj: for immediate mitigation, we should add a kernel-selection heuristic: prefer SEPARATE-backed fused kernels when interleaved_stride >= 128 or dtype==bf16 and seq>=1024. simple pseudocode: 
```
if layout == SEPARATE:
  use fused_fast_kernel()
else: # INTERLEAVED
  if seq < 512:
    use fused_fast_kernel()
  elif dtype == bf16 and stride % 128 == 0:
    use paged_safe_kernel()
  else:
    use fused_with_coalescing_kernel()
```
We can iterate on thresholds after more data.

kevin: also probe alignment: if base_ptr % 256 != 0 then add prefetch padding or fall back. The kernel can check pointer alignment cheaply. Might be easier than changing packing.

sophie: can we add a perf-test in the CI matrix that exercises interleaved strides 64/128/192 and seq 512/1024/2048? would catch regressions early.

perf-bot: nightly-perf: ran new benchmark set for interleaved stride sweep — detected 9.6% regression (fused, seq=2048, stride=128, fp16) vs baseline. Full report uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood/perf/1864501234/interleaved-stride-sweep.html :warning:

maria: thanks — i'll draft a small rollback/patch that restores old packing order behind a feature-flag and add the runtime kernel selection + alignment checks. target: canary tomorrow.

aj: sounds good. also add a lightweight runtime telemetry tag (kernel_choice, stride, alignment, dtype) so we can correlate in console dashboards.

kevin: note — this only shows up on fused-flash variants; paged-flash is more tolerant to non-contiguous heads because it explicitly stages tiles. so our kernel selector should prefer paged for pathological strides.

sophie: i'll open a tiny perf PR with CI cases and the telemetry changes. tagging you both. :thumbsup: 

maria: thanks — will post canary numbers in this thread once up.

aj: one more ask — include a micro-benchmark that simulates the real batching heuristics (small prefix cache hits, then long decode steps) so we don't miss interaction effects between batching + kv-layout.

maria: will add that. quick action items: rollback flag PR, runtime kernel selector, CI regression cases, telemetry.

kevin: accepting — if anyone wants to pair on the alignment guardlet i can help.

sophie: ack.

perf-bot: ci: nightly jobs queued for canary run (expedited).
